[Textbook answer-key error: the key gives mean \(7/3\) and variance \(524/54\); both are impossible. The distribution is symmetric on \(1..6\), which forces the mean to be \(7/2\). And a variable confined to \([1,6]\) has variance at most \((6-1)^{2}/4=6.25\), whereas \(524/54=9.7037\). The correct values are \(7/2\) and \(35/12\).]

[Textbook answer-key error: the key gives variance \(4.9\) and s.d. \(2.21\), which contradict each other — \(2.21^{2}=4.8841\), not 4.9. With \(\sum x=263\) and \(\sum x^{2}=4683\) over 15 values, \(\mathrm{Var}=312.2-(263/15)^{2}=1076/225=4.78222\) and s.d. \(=2.186829\). The key matches neither the population nor the sample variance. The mean \(17.53\) is correct.]

[Textbook answer-key error: the key says "Not a p.d.f.", but it is one. The function is the standard triangular density: \(\int_{0}^{1}x\,dx=1/2\) and \(\int_{1}^{2}(2-x)\,dx=1/2\), totalling exactly 1, and it is non-negative throughout its support (its minimum on each branch is 0). Both defining conditions hold.]

[Textbook answer-key error: the key prints \(4/\log 3\) in the \(E(X)\) slot, but that is \(E(X^{2})\). \(E(X)=2c=2/\log 3=1.82048\); \(E(X^{2})=4c=3.64096\). Two proofs: the support is \((1,3)\) so the mean must lie inside it, and \(3.641>3\); and the key's own variance reconciles only with \(E(X)=2/\log 3\) — using its printed middle value gives a variance of \(-9.6156\), which is impossible. The values of \(c\) and of the variance are correct.]

[Textbook answer-key error in part (ii): the key gives \(25/36,\ 10/36,\ 1/36\). "A six appears on at least one die" is a SINGLE event about the pair — true for 11 of the 36 outcomes — so \(X\in\{0,1\}\) and the distribution is \(25/36,\ 11/36\). The printed key is the number-of-sixes distribution, whose \(X=2\) entry asserts two occurrences of an event that can happen at most once per throw of the pair. Part (i) is correct.]

[Textbook answer-key error in part (ii): the question asks the CONDITIONAL probability \(P(X\leq 3\mid X>0)\), and the key gives \(0.25\) — the numerator alone, undivided. From the book's own c.d.f., \(P(0<X\leq 3)=0.25\) and \(P(X>0)=0.35\), so the answer is \(0.25/0.35=5/7=0.714286\). The p.m.f. row and part (i) are correct, which isolates the defect to the missing division.]
